about: What sink's README and release notes may say about performance. Each claim is a threshold on a metric from bench/run.py, judged on the conservative end of its 95% interval (a '>=' claim must hold for the interval's low end, a '<=' claim for its high end). `bench/run.py claims` re-checks them; `run` checks them after every full run. If a claim fails, the README stops saying it until it passes again. Claims are per machine: a result from a different CPU skips them rather than passing or failing.

claims.claim: sink parses plain text at over 150 MB/s
sink parses colorized output (ls, ripgrep) at over 100 MB/s
sink's parser handles full-screen TUI redraws faster than vte, the parser Alacritty is built on
on plain text, sink's parser is within 25% of vte
a flood of output never takes more than 9ms of a frame: plain text
a flood of output never takes more than 9ms of a frame: TUI redraws
a flood of output never takes more than 9ms of a frame: synchronized updates
while output pours in, sink still takes in over 50 MB/s
a screen of text is finished, GPU included, in under 2ms
with the gel, the CRT effect, HDR text and four panes all on, a frame still fits in a 120Hz refresh
a video background costs under 2ms a frame
a find-bar keystroke at the default 10,000 lines of scrollback takes under 5ms
resizing with 10,000 lines of scrollback rewraps within a 60Hz frame
